physalis-peruviana.name: Physalis peruviana
physalis-peruviana.summary: A South American nightshade plant, called Cape gooseberry or aguaymanto, whose cultivation traces back to the Inca Empire and which later spread worldwide, sometimes becoming invasive.

mzilikazi.name: Mzilikazi
mzilikazi.summary: A Southern African king (c. 1790–1868) who founded the Northern Ndebele, or Matabele, kingdom in what is now Zimbabwe after leading his followers north during the Mfecane.

northern-ndebele-people.name: Ndebele
northern-ndebele-people.summary: Ethnic group native to Zimbabwe, also known as the Amandebele.

shona-people.name: Shona people
shona-people.summary: A Bantu ethnic group native to Southern Africa forming the majority in Zimbabwe, who migrated from the Congo River basin around the end of the first millennium and built a great civilization there.

thomas-baines.name: Thomas Baines
thomas-baines.summary: An English artist and explorer (1820–1875) of colonial southern Africa and Australia.

david-livingstone.name: David Livingstone
david-livingstone.summary: A Scottish doctor, missionary and explorer (1813–1873) famed for seeking the source of the Nile in Africa and for campaigning against the East African slave trade.

knobkerrie.name: Knobkerrie
knobkerrie.summary: A wooden club with a large knob at one end, used mainly in Southern and Eastern Africa for fighting, carrying marked cultural and political significance.

mashonaland.name: Mashonaland
mashonaland.summary: A region in northeastern Zimbabwe, home to nearly half the country's population and mostly settled by the Shona people, including the capital Harare.

john-guille-millais.name: John Guille Millais
john-guille-millais.summary: British artist, naturalist and travel writer specializing in wildlife and flower portraiture, noted for exact illustrations made during extensive late-Victorian travels.

nyamazana.name: Nyamazana
nyamazana.summary: An Ngoni warrior-queen active during the mid-19th-century Mfecane migrations in southern Africa.

rozvi-empire.name: Rozvi Empire
rozvi-empire.summary: A Shona state on the Zimbabwean Plateau (c. 1683–1866) established by Changamire Dombo, whose name reflects a legacy as a warrior nation; it became the most powerful fighting force in Zimbabwe.

matabeleland.name: Matabeleland
matabeleland.summary: A region of southwestern Zimbabwe named for its Ndebele ('Amatabele') inhabitants, home to the capital Bulawayo and rich in coal and gold deposits.

shaka.name: Shaka
shaka.summary: King of the Zulu Kingdom from 1816 to 1828 who reorganized its military system; his reign coincided with the start of the Mfecane, a period of widespread upheaval in southern Africa.

pedro-v-of-kongo.name: Pedro V of Kongo
pedro-v-of-kongo.summary: King of Kongo from 1859 until his death in 1891, based in the district of Madimba, south of the capital, in lands held by the ancient southern Kinlaza lineage called Kivuzi.

lvaro-xiii-of-kongo.name: Álvaro XIII of Kongo
lvaro-xiii-of-kongo.summary: King of Kongo from 1857 to 1859, a member of the Nkanga branch of the Kimpanzu house, who died in 1875.

m-banza-kongo.name: Mbanza Kongo
m-banza-kongo.summary: Capital of the Kingdom of Kongo from before Portuguese contact in 1483 until 1915; now a city in Angola and a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2017.

danamombe.name: Danamombe
danamombe.summary: A Zimbabwean archaeological site near Gweru whose stone ruins resemble those of Khami, close to the smaller Naletale ruins.

jameson-raid.name: Jameson Raid
jameson-raid.summary: Failed 1895–96 raid on the South African Republic by colonial administrator Leander Starr Jameson, meant to spark an uprising against President Paul Kruger; it embarrassed Britain and helped cause the Second Boer War.

first-chimurenga.name: First Chimurenga
first-chimurenga.summary: Conflict fought 1896–1897 in what became Rhodesia (now Zimbabwe), beginning as a Matabele uprising against the British South Africa Company and later joined by the Shona; also called the Second Matabele War.

frederick-russell-burnham.name: Frederick Russell Burnham
frederick-russell-burnham.summary: American scout and adventurer who served the British in colonial Africa and taught woodcraft to Robert Baden-Powell, helping inspire the Scouting Movement.

bulawayo-zulu-empire.name: Kwa-Bulawayo
bulawayo-zulu-empire.summary: Royal kraal of Shaka Zulu and capital of the early Zulu Empire, founded around 1820 after Shaka's conquest of the Ndwandwe kingdom and the site of his first contact with European traders.

zulu-kingdom.name: Zulu Kingdom
zulu-kingdom.summary: A Southern African monarchy built by Shaka in the 1810s that ruled a wide stretch of coast, later fighting Britain in the 1879 Anglo-Zulu War before being absorbed into the Colony of Natal.

ndwandwe.name: Ndwandwe
ndwandwe.summary: A Bantu Nguni-speaking people, also known as the Nxumalo, whose kingdom was conquered by Shaka around 1820; today found across South Africa, Mozambique, Eswatini, and Zimbabwe.

chimurenga.name: Chimurenga
chimurenga.summary: A Shona word for 'revolutionary struggle,' used for uprisings against British South Africa Company rule in the 1890s and the 1960s-70s war against Rhodesia's white government.

cecil-rhodes.name: Cecil Rhodes
cecil-rhodes.summary: British mining magnate and politician who served as Prime Minister of the Cape Colony from 1890 to 1896, and whose British South Africa Company founded Rhodesia.

bhunu.name: Bhunu (Ngwane V)
bhunu.summary: King of Swaziland, reigning as Ngwane V, from 1895 until his death in 1899; he was a son of King Mbandzeni.

sobhuza-ii.name: Sobhuza II
sobhuza-ii.summary: King of Swaziland (now Eswatini) for over 82 years, from 1899 until his death in 1982, the longest verified reign of any monarch.

thomas-mofolo.name: Thomas Mofolo
thomas-mofolo.summary: Often called the first African novelist (1876–1948), he wrote in Sesotho, best known for Chaka, a retelling of Zulu king Shaka's rise and fall.

sotho-language.name: Sesotho
sotho-language.summary: A Southern Bantu language, also called Sesotho, spoken as the national language of Lesotho and an official language of South Africa.

izibongo.name: Izibongo
izibongo.summary: A genre of oral literature among Bantu peoples of Southern Africa, such as the Zulu and Xhosa, often called praise poetry though it can include criticism too.

chaka-novel.name: Chaka (novel)
chaka-novel.summary: The third and final novel by Lesotho writer Thomas Mofolo, retelling in Sesotho the rise and fall of the Zulu king Shaka; published in 1925 after a 15-year delay, with an English translation in 1931.

colony-of-natal.name: Colony of Natal
colony-of-natal.summary: A former British colony in south-eastern Africa, proclaimed in 1843 and merged into the Union of South Africa in 1910; now the province of KwaZulu-Natal.

marie-corelli.name: Marie Corelli
marie-corelli.summary: English novelist (1855–1924) whose bestselling fiction, beginning with A Romance of Two Worlds in 1886, dealt with Christianity, reincarnation and mysticism despite frequent critical ridicule.

henry-morton-stanley.name: Henry Morton Stanley
henry-morton-stanley.summary: Welsh-American explorer and journalist famed for finding missionary David Livingstone in Central Africa and for later work mapping the Congo for King Leopold II of Belgium.

lualaba-river.name: Lualaba River
lualaba-river.summary: River in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo that supplies the greatest streamflow to the Congo River, even though the Chambeshi is recognized as its official source.

nyangwe.name: Nyangwe
nyangwe.summary: A town on the Lualaba River in the Congo, founded around 1860 as an Arab trading depot and a major 19th-century centre of the ivory and slave trade.

william-holman-bentley.name: William Holman Bentley
william-holman-bentley.summary: English Baptist missionary in the Congo (1855–1905).

kongo-language.name: Kikongo
kongo-language.summary: A Bantu language of the Kongo people spoken by around seven million people in Central Africa, historically carried across the Atlantic by enslaved Africans.

tippu-tip.name: Tippu Tip
tippu-tip.summary: Arab-Omani trader and explorer (c. 1832–1905) who built a major slave and ivory trading network in Central Africa while nominally loyal to the Sultan of Zanzibar.

albertine-rift.name: Albertine Rift
albertine-rift.summary: Western branch of the East African Rift, running from Lake Albert to Lake Tanganyika through Uganda, DR Congo, Rwanda, Burundi and Tanzania.

kanem-bornu-empire.name: Kanem-Bornu Empire
kanem-bornu-empire.summary: A long-lived empire around Lake Chad, founded around 700 CE and sustained by trans-Saharan trade, later re-centered from Kanem to the Bornu region after the 14th century.

girgam.name: Girgam
girgam.summary: The royal chronicle of the Kanem-Bornu Empire, written in Arabic, listing 69 rulers and details of their reigns; discovered by traveller Heinrich Barth in 1851.

heinrich-barth.name: Heinrich Barth
heinrich-barth.summary: German explorer of Africa (1821–1865), regarded as one of the greatest European explorers of the continent for his careful documentation of cultures and oral histories.

parfait-louis-monteil.name: Parfait-Louis Monteil
parfait-louis-monteil.summary: A French colonial military officer and explorer who, between 1890 and 1892, travelled from Senegal east to Lake Chad and then north across the Sahara to Tripoli.

say-niger.name: Say, Niger
say-niger.summary: A town in southwest Niger on the Niger River, once a small Songhai settlement turned into a center of Islamic learning in the 19th century by the Fulani marabout Alfa Mohamed Diobo.

kingdom-of-kongo.name: Kingdom of Kongo
kingdom-of-kongo.summary: A Central African kingdom spanning parts of modern Angola, Congo and Gabon, independent from around 1390 to 1862, later a Portuguese vassal until its monarchy was abolished in 1914.

portuguese-angola.name: Portuguese Angola
portuguese-angola.summary: The Portuguese colony that became Angola, held from 1575 until independence in 1975, initially confined to the coast before expanding inland in the 18th and 19th centuries.

gaza-empire.name: Gaza Empire
gaza-empire.summary: An African empire founded by Soshangane in 1824 in what is now southern Mozambique and southeastern Zimbabwe, reaching its height in the 1860s before collapsing after defeat by the Portuguese in 1895.

soshangane.name: Soshangane
soshangane.summary: Founder and first ruler of the Gaza Empire, reigning from 1825 until his death around 1858, with a realm stretching from the Limpopo to the Zambezi rivers.

manuel-iii-of-kongo.name: Manuel III of Kongo
manuel-iii-of-kongo.summary: The last Manikongo, or ruler, of the Kingdom of Kongo, reigning as a Portuguese vassal from 1911 to 1914, born Manuel Martins Kiditu in 1872 and dying in 1927.

manikongo.name: Manikongo
manikongo.summary: The title of the ruler of the Kingdom of Kongo (14th–19th centuries), who appointed provincial governors and received tribute, ruling from the capital Mbanza Kongo.

congo-free-state.name: Congo Free State
congo-free-state.summary: A state in Central Africa from 1885 to 1908, privately owned as an absolute monarchy by King Leopold II of Belgium and later notorious for atrocities against Indigenous people.

mawewe.name: Mawewe
mawewe.summary: King of the Gaza Empire in 1859, son of King Soshangane, whose expansionist rule and conflict with his half-brother Mzila over the throne ended in his defeat.

mzila.name: Mzila
mzila.summary: King of the Gaza Empire in southern Mozambique from 1861 to 1885, son of its founder Soshangane, whom he succeeded after defeating his brother Mawewe.

manjacaze.name: Manjakazi
manjacaze.summary: A town in Gaza province, southern Mozambique, serving as the administrative center of Manjacaze District; also known as Mandlakazi.

andr-ii-of-kongo.name: André II of Kongo
andr-ii-of-kongo.summary: King of Kongo from 1830 to 1842 and first child of King Garcia V, who was overthrown in 1842 by Henrique III but survived without regaining the throne.

garcia-v-of-kongo.name: Garcia V of Kongo
garcia-v-of-kongo.summary: Ruler of the Kingdom of Kongo from 1803 until his death in 1830, who restored the throne to the Água Rosada dynasty founded by Pedro IV.

henrique-iii-of-kongo.name: Henrique III of Kongo
henrique-iii-of-kongo.summary: Ruler of the Kingdom of Kongo from 1842 to 1857, who seized the throne by overthrowing his predecessor and built power through networks of followers.

luanda.name: Luanda
luanda.summary: Capital and largest city of Angola, founded by the Portuguese in 1576, which served as a center of the slave trade to Brazil before it was prohibited.

hu-la-province.name: Huíla
hu-la-province.summary: A province of Angola whose capital is Lubango, known for basket-making from reeds.

lvaro-xiv-of-kongo.name: Álvaro XIV of Kongo
lvaro-xiv-of-kongo.summary: Ruler of Kongo from February 1891 to 1896, whose father had signed the kingdom's vassalage to Portugal in 1888.

kongo-people.name: Kongo people
kongo-people.summary: A Bantu ethnic group and speakers of Kikongo who lived along the Atlantic coast in the kingdoms of Kongo, Loango and Kakongo, and were among the first Africans to meet Portuguese traders in 1483.

nzambi-ampungu.name: Nzambi Ampungu
nzambi-ampungu.summary: The Supreme God and eternal Sky Father of traditional Kongo spirituality, associated with the sun; his female counterpart rules the moon. After Portuguese colonization he became identified with the Christian God.

chokwe-people.name: Chokwe
chokwe-people.summary: A Bantu ethnic group of Central and Southern Africa, found mainly in Angola, the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Zambia, known for varied traditional artwork.

ambundu.name: Ambundu
ambundu.summary: A Bantu people on a plateau in present-day Angola, speaking Kimbundu and forming about a quarter of Angola's population.

kongo-cosmogram.name: Dikenga (Kongo cosmogram)
kongo-cosmogram.summary: A core symbol of Kongo religion showing the physical and spiritual worlds, the sun's rotation, and the four stages of life, drawn as a cross within a circle.

nganga.name: Nganga
nganga.summary: A spiritual healer, diviner and ritual specialist in traditional Kongo religion, also found among descendants of Kongo and Mbundu peoples across the African diaspora, including Brazil, Cuba and Haiti.

john-thornton-historian.name: John Thornton
john-thornton-historian.summary: American historian (born 1949) at Boston University specializing in African, African Diaspora and Atlantic World history.

linda-heywood.name: Linda Heywood
linda-heywood.summary: Caribbean-American historian specializing in African, especially Angolan, history; co-author with her husband John Thornton of award-winning work on Central Africans and the Atlantic world.

bulawayo.name: Bulawayo
bulawayo.summary: Second-largest city in Zimbabwe, founded around 1840 as the royal kraal of Ndebele king Mzilikazi and later ruled by his son Lobengula until British forces captured it in 1893.

rhodesia.name: Rhodesia
rhodesia.summary: An unrecognized state in southern Africa from 1965 to 1979, formed when its white-minority government declared independence from Britain, later becoming Zimbabwe.

harare.name: Salisbury
harare.summary: Former name of Harare, capital of Zimbabwe; founded in 1890 by the British South Africa Company and named after British Prime Minister Lord Salisbury, before being renamed in 1982.

gweru.name: Gweru (Gwelo)
gweru.summary: Capital of Zimbabwe's Midlands Province, founded in 1894 as a military outpost and formerly known as Gwelo.

mhondoro.name: Mhondoro
mhondoro.summary: Royal ancestral spirits in Shona traditional religion believed to mediate between God and people; cults centered on them helped organize resistance during Zimbabwe's First and Second Chimurengas.

mwari.name: Mwari
mwari.summary: The supreme creator deity in Shona and Venda traditional religion, believed to be the author of all things and all life, worshipped mainly in Mozambique, South Africa and Zimbabwe.

nehanda-charwe-nyakasikana.name: Nehanda
nehanda-charwe-nyakasikana.summary: A revered female ancestral spirit (mhondoro) of the Zezuru Shona people, whose medium is said to have helped lead a revolt against British colonisation in 1896.

kingdom-of-loango.name: Kingdom of Loango
kingdom-of-loango.summary: A Kongo-founded state on Africa's Atlantic coast from roughly the 1500s to 1800s, exporting copper and cloth, at its height reaching from Cape St Catherine near the Congo River's mouth.

vili-people.name: Vili people
vili-people.summary: A Central African Bantu ethnic group and subgroup of the Kongo people, found in Gabon, the Republic of Congo, Cabinda and the DRC, historically part of the Kingdom of Loango and known for its matrilineal society and nail-fetish nkisi carvings.
